title: Arabesque No. 1 in E Major
source: Mutopia Project, https://www.mutopiaproject.org/cgibin/piece-info.cgi?id=1777, typeset by Keith OHara, source Durand et Fils (1904) (Public Domain)

musicalLanguage.description: This Mutopia typeset of Debussy's Arabesque No. 1 runs 106 measures at 144 BPM in 4/4 time with 1,448 notes. The stated E major fits the content strongly (statedKeyFit 0.802); content-based detection names A major only at a weak 0.081 margin, below the analysis's own mismatch floor, so harmony claims stay with E major. Eleven structural regions span the piece; the sharpest boundary opens at measure 71 (novelty 8.286), which is the recapitulation. A 132-note right-hand span (measures 2-18) restates at measures 72-88 (moderate evidence, coverage 0.361), independently corroborated by a 44-note left-hand span (measures 9-18 restated at 79-88) and by twelve byte-identical measure pairs (3/73, 4/74, 5/75, 6/76, 8/78, 10/80, 11/81, 12/82, 13/83, 14/84, 15/85, 16/86). Implied E-major windows are the most-cited gated label (7 windows, 6.2% coverage), including the close at measure 106; F#m7 appears at both measure 3 and its recap counterpart measure 73. Labels cover 23% of measures — the rest did not clear the confidence gate, typical of this arpeggiated texture rather than evidence of silence.
musicalLanguage.structure: Eleven structural regions from the section-lens pass. The opening region (measures 1-5) leads into the first flowing page (measures 6-17, novelty 2.51); a 23-note left-hand span covering measures 1-7 restates at 71-77 when the recap begins. Inside the middle, measures 41-46 restate at 57-62 (byte-identical pairs 41/57, 42/58, 43/59, 45/61, 46/62), and a 23-note right-hand cell at measures 47-49 returns at 51-53. A 4-measure left-hand rest gap occupies measures 67-70 immediately before the recap. The recap region itself is measures 71-86 (novelty 8.286), after which measures 87-94, 95-99, and 100-106 close the piece. The busiest bars are 93, 99, and 101 (18-19 onsets); the sparsest include measures 38 and 68 (2 onsets, left hand silent) and the final measure 106. The right hand's highest pitch is G#6 at measure 105; the left hand's lowest is E1 at measure 37.
keyMoments: The recapitulation at measures 71-88 restates the opening material from measures 2-18 almost exactly, confirmed independently by the 132-note right-hand span, the 44-note left-hand span, and twelve byte-identical measure pairs (3/73 through 16/86) — a textbook example of how a return of the opening theme creates large-scale unity even in a piece as fluid as this one.

The stated E major fits the content strongly (statedKeyFit 0.802) even though a weak detection names A major at 0.081 margin — this teaches an important listening skill: trust the gated windows (E is the most-cited label, and measure 106 itself is E) rather than a below-floor whole-song guess.

A rolling right-hand figure at measures 17, 71, and 87 is byte-identical at all three points, sitting at the edges of the recapitulation — recognizing it once teaches the hinge into the return and the hinge out of it.

The inner repeat at measures 47-49 returning at 51-53 (23-note right-hand cell, coverage 0.065) plus the 41-46 / 57-62 restatement demonstrate a single middle-section idea doing structural work twice, framed by implied A-major and E-major windows at measures 42/58 and 46/62.
teachingGoals: Practice the opening material (measures 2-18) and its recapitulation (measures 72-88) side by side — learning them as the same passage, not two different sections, builds the piece far faster.

Listen for the implied E-major windows recurring through the piece (7 gated windows, including the close at measure 106) and the F#m7 color at measures 3 and 73, and develop comfort with a texture whose harmony is gated sparsely because of continuous arpeggios.
Recognize the rolling right-hand figure at measures 17, 71, and 87 as one repeated shape — practice it once and apply it at all three locations.
Build evenness in the arpeggiated texture, especially through the busiest bars 93, 99, and 101, since the flowing character depends on those onsets staying smooth rather than heavy.
styleTips: Let the arpeggios shimmer rather than pound — listen for the rolling right-hand figures staying light even as they recur across the recapitulation at measures 72-88.
Pedal generously but change with each shift in the implied harmony (E, A, F#m7, C#m7) — listen for the color changing smoothly as the analysis's chord windows move between roots.

Balance the melody so it floats on top of the arpeggiated texture rather than getting buried in it — listen for the top line staying audible through the busiest triplet passages at measures 93, 99, and 101.

Treat the recapitulation at measures 71-88 as a return, not a repeat — listen for it carrying the memory of the middle-section restatements at 41-62, even though the notes of the opening page come back nearly identical.
